extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX / PGF/TikZ users and package authors writing custom nodes, shapes, and arrow tips
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for creating and using PGF/TikZ arrow tip kinds, nodes, anchors, and custom shapes (including saved anchors, node parts, layers, and shape-size parameters). Focused on authors of TikZ/pgf graphics and custom shape declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defining combined arrow tip kinds
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \pgfarrowsdeclarecombine (and the * variant) to create a new arrow kind that combines two existing arrow kinds; the first is the innermost, the second the outermost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The code for the combined arrow kind installs a canvas translation before the innermost arrow is drawn so the right tip of the innermost arrow touches the right end of the outermost arrow. An optional offset argument can increase or decrease the distance between the inner and outermost arrow. A star variant places the line end inside the innermost arrow. Examples show \pgfarrowsdeclarecombine and shortcut double/triple declare commands (\pgfarrowsdeclaredouble, \pgfarrowsdeclaretriple).

rubrics_metrics.name: Installing arrow tip kinds for strokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \pgfsetarrowsstart{<start-kind>} and \pgfsetarrowsend{<end-kind>} to install arrow tips that will be used for subsequent strokes in the current TeX group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the argument is empty, no arrow tips are drawn at that end. \pgfsetarrows{<start>-<end>} calls both start and end setters. Examples show \pgfsetarrows{latex-to} and \pgfsetarrowsstart{latex}. Warning: when compatibility mode is active, old commands \pgfsetstartarrow and \pgfsetendarrow exist but are incompatible with the meta-arrow management; avoid mixing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know predefined arrow tip kinds
rubrics_metrics.description: PGF/TikZ provides a set of arrow tip kinds that are always defined (e.g., stealth-stealth, to-to, latex-latex, |-|, and their reversed variants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentation lists these predefined kinds and shows that both 'thick' and 'thin' variants are yielded for them. For further arrow tips see other documentation pages (referenced).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create nodes with \pgfnode or \pgfmultipartnode and remember positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Create nodes using \pgfnode (single-part) or \pgfmultipartnode (multi-part); these macros draw the shape at a position and remember the node's position within the current {pgfpicture}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate transformations are fully supported for remembered positions (so transformed positions are correctly determined). Canvas transformations are not supported for remembered positions. If no name is given to \pgfnode, nothing is saved for later reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anchor usage for placement and referencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Anchors are important named positions of shapes (e.g., center, north, text) used both when creating a node (to place it) and when referencing it later (you always reference an anchor of a node).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating a node you specify which anchor of the shape should lie at the placement point (e.g., north at origin places node below origin). When referencing, you always ask for a node's anchor (e.g., north anchor of the node) which returns a coordinate. When coordinate transformations were in force at creation, all anchors are transformed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand shape drawing layers and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: Shapes may draw up to seven distinct layers (behind the background, background path, before background, label, behind foreground, foreground path, before foreground).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each layer has a role (e.g., label layer inserts text; background path drawn before label). Which layers a shape uses depends on the shape. Use appropriate layer commands when declaring shapes to control drawing order and whether things appear behind or in front of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare and manage node parts properly
rubrics_metrics.description: If a shape has multiple text labels (node parts), declare them with \nodeparts{<list>} and set up a TEX box \pgfnodepart<partname>box for each part before calling \pgfmultipartnode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a multipart node is created, the boxes are placed at the corresponding anchors for each part. To conserve TeX box registers, multiple shapes may reuse the same box (use \newbox and \let to alias). For part names containing spaces, create an alias via \expandafter\let with \csname.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \pgftransformresetnontranslations when needed
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want coordinate transformations to affect the anchor position where a node is placed but do not want the shape itself to be transformed, call \pgftransformresetnontranslations prior to \pgfnode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show rotating and shifting the coordinate system but resetting non-translation components so text/shape are not rotated while placement is affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set shape size and separation recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Use commands like \pgfsetshapeminwidth, \pgfsetshapeminheight, \pgfsetshapeinnerxsep, \pgfsetshapeinnerysep, \pgfsetshapeouterxsep, \pgfsetshapeouterysep, and \pgfsetshapeaspect to recommend shape minimum sizes, inner/outer separations, and aspect ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These commands set macros (e.g., \pgfshapeminwidth) that shapes may use as recommendations when computing sizes and anchors. Note: these are only recommendations — shapes may choose to ignore them. Examples illustrate how min width and inner/outer separations affect anchor positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference anchors in the same picture with \pgfpointanchor and be aware of transform behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \pgfpointanchor{<node>}{<anchor>} to return the coordinate of a node's anchor in the current picture; \pgfpointanchor takes the current transformation matrix into account by applying the inverse transform before returning the anchor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because \pgfpointanchor applies an inverse transform, calling it while transformations are active will return coordinates that appear not to be additionally transformed; if you need the transformed anchor, invoke \pgfpointanchor with no transformations in force (for example, reset transforms and save the resulting coordinate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use \pgfpointshapeborder to get border points (may be simplified)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use \pgfpointshapeborder{<node>}{<point>} to get the point on the border of a shape that lies on the line from the center to <point>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex shapes, the returned point may lie on a border of a 'simplified' version of the shape, so it is not guaranteed to be precisely on the original complex border. The border anchor computation is shape-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing anchors across pictures requires position tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: To reference anchors of nodes defined in other pictures you must enable picture position remembering and use a backend that supports position tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: (1) Use a backend driver that supports position tracking (pdfTeX does; dvips currently does not). (2) Say \pgfrememberpicturepositiononpagetrue somewhere before or inside every picture in which you wish to reference a node and from which you wish to reference a node in another picture. (3) Run TeX twice (position info may be written to an external file on the first run). (4) Switch off automatic bounding box computations for the picture (use \pgfusepath{use as bounding box}) so nodes from other pictures do not affect the current picture's bounding box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not redefine special predefined nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: Several special nodes are always defined and should not be redeclared: 'current bounding box', 'current path bounding box', and 'current page'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'current bounding box' is a rectangle node whose size reflects the bounding box of the current picture (anchors like south east return corners). 'current path bounding box' reflects the current path. 'current page' is inside a virtual remembered picture whose size is the current page — useful for absolute page positioning (works only with supporting backends).

rubrics_metrics.name: What must be provided when declaring a new shape
rubrics_metrics.description: When declaring a new shape you must provide: a shape name, code for computing saved anchors and saved dimensions, code for computing anchor positions (in terms of saved anchors), and optionally code for background/foreground paths, before/behind layers, and a list of node parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shapes must be flexible and efficient: saved anchors and dimensions should record only the minimal necessary data to allow many normal anchors to be derived later without heavy per-node storage or computation. Use \pgfdeclareshape{<name>}{<spec>} to declare a shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer saved anchors for efficiency; normal anchors computed on demand
rubrics_metrics.description: Saved anchors are computed and stored when a node is created; normal anchors are computed only when requested and can reference saved anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design shapes to compute a small set of saved anchors/dimensions (e.g., rectangle saves northeast and southwest) and express other anchors (north, west, etc.) in terms of these saved anchors to minimize memory and computation overhead when many nodes exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use shape-declaration commands correctly (savedanchor, saveddimen, anchor, anchorborder, backgroundpath, foregroundpath)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within a \pgfdeclareshape specification use the provided special commands: \savedanchor to compute and record a point (must set \pgf@x and \pgf@y or call \pgfpoint), \saveddimen/\shapedimen to record numeric values, \anchor to define a publicly accessible anchor (its code must set \pgf@x and \pgf@y), \anchorborder to compute a border point given an input, and \backgroundpath / \foregroundpath to provide path construction code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: \savedanchor code is executed when a node is created and the node part boxes are available (so you can use \wd/\ht/\dp of boxes); \savedanchor should set \pgf@x and \pgf@y (or use \pgfpoint). \anchor code executes on demand and may call saved-anchor macros. \anchorborder receives the point (in \pgf@x/\pgf@y) and must set them to the correct border point (often by calling helper functions like \pgfpointborderrectangle). Background/foreground path code is executed with saved anchors defined and should contain path construction commands (these paths may be stroked, filled, or discarded depending on node usage).
